row.scim_price_text: Control: $18/member/mo (annual), as low as $9 with Expensify Card; Custom pricing
row.evidence: Expensify's pricing page lists SAML/SSO only under Control ("Custom pricing as low as $9 per active member/month"), and the help centre says the Okta SCIM API for account deprovisioning is set up "Once SAML is configured" by requesting SCIM API access via concierge@expensify.com.
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated). Pricing page now shows Control as 'Custom pricing, as low as $9 per active member/month'; the help-centre pricing table gives Control annual $18/member/mo standard ($9 with Expensify Card), pay-per-use $36 ($18 with Card), and Collect $5 per unique member/mo pay-per-use. Numeric SCIM price now uses the $18 annual standard price instead of June's Card-discounted $9, so the multiplier moves from 1.8 to 3.6 without a price change. SCIM is Okta-only, needs SAML first and manual activation via Concierge, and Expensify describes it as for account deprovisioning; its Okta Workflows article says the native Okta integration does not provision or update users (Okta's OIN page shows Create/Update/Deactivate). Provisioning beyond that is via the Advanced Employee Updater API.

plans.name: Control
plans.price_text: Annual: $18 per member/month (as low as $9 with Expensify Card); pay-per-use $36 per active member/month

auth.token_source: SCIM token issued by Expensify on request via concierge@expensify.com, pasted into Okta provisioning settings
auth.notes: Expensify calls it a 'SCIM token'; method assumed bearer-style token entered in Okta.

operations.notes: Expensify documents the SCIM API 'for account deprovisioning' and says the native Okta integration does not provision or update users; Okta's OIN markup checks Create, Update and Deactivate.

deprovision.data_retained: Closed domain accounts can be reopened by reinviting the user (manual close behaviour; SCIM-specific behaviour not documented).

limitations.text: Okta only; requires SAML to be configured first and SCIM API access requested from Concierge.
Expensify says its native Okta integration does not provision or update users; user creation/updates go through Okta Workflows plus the Advanced Employee Updater API.

auth.notes: partnerUserID + partnerUserSecret generated in the Integrations Center; OAuth2 partner auth is private beta.

capabilities.notes: Users are provisioned into workspaces (policies); isTerminated removes them from the policy. Domain groups can be assigned but not created. Policy getter returns policy employees.

endpoints.purpose: Single RPC endpoint; requestJobDescription type 'update' with inputSettings.type 'employees' runs the Advanced Employee Updater (provision, update, isTerminated de-provision, role, domain group)
type 'get' with inputSettings.type 'policyList' / 'policy' returns policies and their employees

rate_limits.text: Up to 5 requests every 10 seconds and 20 requests every 60 seconds; 429 when exceeded

limitations.text: Domain groups cannot be created via the API, only assigned.

okta.notes: OIN markup checks SAML, SWA, SCIM and Create/Update/Deactivate; Expensify says SCIM is for deprovisioning and must be requested.

entra.notes: Entra gallery SSO tutorial only; no Expensify provisioning tutorial (404).

google.notes: Expensify Google Workspace Marketplace app with manual 'Sync G Suite Now' to add users to a workspace.

onelogin.notes: Expensify's SAML guide lists OneLogin; OneLogin catalogue not loaded.

fallbacks.other_sync: Google Apps manual sync; Advanced Employee Updater API (HRIS feeds, Okta Workflows); Workday/Certinia HR integrations on Control

conflicts.text: Expensify's Okta Workflows article says the native Okta integration does not provision or update users, while its SAML article documents an Okta SCIM API and Okta's OIN page checks SCIM Create/Update/Deactivate.
Pricing page: Control 'as low as $9 per active member/month'; help-centre table: Control annual $18 per member standard, as low as $9 only with the Expensify Card.

open_questions: SCIM version, base URL, endpoints, attributes, filtering, pagination and rate limits are not published.
Whether SCIM creates/updates users or only deprovisions is contradictory across Expensify and Okta pages.
What SCIM deprovisioning does exactly (close account vs remove from workspace) and whether it stops billing is not documented.
Which plan is needed to generate API credentials / use the Advanced Employee Updater is not stated.
Whether SAML sign-in creates accounts just-in-time is not documented.
No audit-log API or user-event webhooks found.
